messages:
Alice Garcia: quick sync — AtlasPay (fintech) is on a 1yr deal, asking for Net45 payment terms + 50% annual upfront. They're asking for an invoice split we haven't done often. POC next week, SEs already engaged. list price $240k, they're pushing for a 25% discount tied to a 1yr commit. can deal desk / finance weigh in?

Ben Kline: thanks. can you paste the exact invoice schedule they want and confirmation of discount ask? also need AR contact and whether they'll provide a PO.

Alice Garcia: copying proposed schedule from the customer thread:
```
Year 1 total: $240,000 list
Requested discount: 25% -> $180,000
Invoice schedule requested:
  - 50% upfront on signature: $90,000
  - 25% on go-live (POC -> prod): $45,000
  - 25% 6 months after go-live: $45,000
Payment term on invoices: Net45
```
They will sign an SOW and provide a PO. AR contact is maria.lopez@atlaspay.com. POC deliverables look standard (LLM-powered risk scoring).

Maya Patel: POC timeline ok — we'll need sandbox access and a subset of their data. no extra infra costs. if we do a 25% discount for committed capacity we should gate the final payment on a successful rollout.

Ian Cho: Net45 is doable but requires a credit check for new customers. default policy is Net30; Net45 needs VP Finance approval or a signed credit app. also note revenue recognition: if they pay 50% upfront we need clear SOW dates to recognize MRR properly.

Sam Rivera (Finance): +1 to Ian. If they provide a PO and credit looks clean we can accept Net45 for 1yr but we need to log payment terms in billing system and add a 1.5% admin fee for Net45 on top of standard terms (we use this to offset AR costs). Is sales ok with fee?

Alice Garcia: fee will be a negotiation point; AtlasPay said cash flow is tight so they probably won't accept more fees. can deal desk consider approval without fee if legal signs stronger commitments?

Ben Kline: proposal from deal desk: two options to present to customer — pick one:
1) Standard concession: 25% commitment discount -> $180k. Accept Net30. Invoice schedule can be split as requested but with Net30. No admin fee.
2) Earned concession: Accept Net45 + requested split, but only after completed credit check and with a signed SOW + 2% admin fee OR escrow for 50% upfront to mitigate risk. Also require legal to approve an automatic payment fallback clause.
Which should I present?

Maya Patel: option 2 sounds heavy. for speed of deal (they want POC next week) option 1 gets us moving faster. we can still do rollback/upgrade logic in SOW.

Ian Cho: if you go option 1 finance can move fast. option 2 takes 3–5 business days for credit and legal signoff.

Alice Garcia: customer priority is to get the POC started asap. I'll present option 1 first (Net30, same split). If they push Net45 I can escalate.

invoicing-bot: Reminder: create invoice schedule in Billing with the following draft if option 1 chosen:
```
Invoice 1: On signature - 50% of $180,000 -> $90,000, terms Net30
Invoice 2: On go-live - 25% -> $45,000, terms Net30
Invoice 3: 6 months after go-live - 25% -> $45,000, terms Net30
Billing notes: PO# from AtlasPay required. Revenue will be recognized per SOW dates.
```

Ben Kline: thanks — Alice, once you confirm which option they accept tag @Ben Kline and @Sam Rivera so we can finalize deal desk ticket and billing entries. I'll draft a short approval note for legal if they push Net45. :thumbsup:

Alice Garcia: will update after POC kickoff call tomorrow morning. thanks all! :rocket:
